newsitem.title: CANADA: Hudson's Bay unit plans to close a facility.
newsitem.headline: Hudson's Bay unit plans to close a facility.

text.p: Zellers, a discount department store chain owned by Hudson's Bay Co said on Wednesday it plans to close a major distribution center in Montreal, a move that would affect 379 jobs.
Zellers, which is based in Montreal but is moving its head office to Toronto where its parent company is based, said it will close its 450,000 square-foot distribution centre in Montreal North.
The closing is part of an ongoing effort to maximize the efficiency of the company's distribution channels, Zellers said.

Zellers said that after closing several several obsolete facilities in Vancouver, Calgary, Edmonton, Toronto and Ottawa, 15 highly-efficient distribution depots have been opened across Canada, including three in Quebec in the past two years.

Zellers said the Montreal North facility had become outdated and would close it as soon as possible. The company said it hopes to minimize the impact on the center's 379 employees with early retirement, severance packages and individual counselling. ((Reuters Montreal bureau 514-985-2434))
